s.description: Evaluate and enforce testing patterns including judge validation (meta-testing), UAT generation for human review, BDD Cucumber-to-Playwright pipeline, and test quality across all layers

scope.directories: tests/, e2e/, features/, steps/, playwright/, __tests__/, specs/, fixtures/

testing_system.requirement: MANDATORY: Tests must be human-verifiable, behavior-driven where possible, and structured to expose judge violations rather than confirm happy paths

spec_document.auto_create: If not exists, create comprehensive testing architecture spec
spec_document.format:
## Testing Philosophy - Tests exist to BREAK things, not confirm they work - UAT is written for HUMAN validation, not rubber-stamping - BDD features are the single source of truth for user-facing behavior - AI-generated tests are PROPOSALS, never trusted without human review
## Test Layers | Layer | Tool | Owns | Trust Level | |-------|------|------|-------------| | Unit | Vitest/Jest | Pure logic, utils, transforms | Machine-verified | | Integration | Vitest + MSW/testcontainers | Service boundaries, API contracts | Machine-verified | | Component | Playwright CT / Testing Library | UI behavior, accessibility | Machine-verified | | E2E | Playwright | Critical user flows | Machine-verified, human-reviewed | | UAT | Playwright (generated) | Business acceptance | HUMAN-VERIFIED ONLY | | Judge Validation | Custom harness | Judge accuracy | Human-reviewed |
## BDD Pipeline - Feature files (.feature) → Step definitions (.steps.ts) → Playwright execution - Feature files are human-authored or human-approved - Step definitions may be AI-generated but must map 1:1 to feature steps - No orphan steps, no orphan features
## UAT Generation Rules - UAT is ALWAYS presented as a checklist for human execution - UAT includes expected screenshots/states for visual verification - UAT NEVER auto-passes; human must explicitly mark pass/fail - UAT covers edge cases the developer didn't think of
## Judge Validation - Each judge XML has corresponding adversarial test cases - Tests attempt to FOOL the judge with code that looks compliant but isn't - Tests verify the judge catches all documented anti-patterns - False positive rate tracked per judge
## Connected Systems - Cross-reference: All other *-specs.md (tests validate judge criteria) - Cross-reference: design-specs.md (visual regression in UAT) - Cross-reference: state-specs.md (state-related test scenarios)

architecture_principles.principle: AI generates test proposals. Humans approve, reject, or modify. No test is trusted simply because it passes.
Good tests try to break the system. If all your tests pass on the first run, your tests are weak.
Feature files are the shared language between PM, dev, and QA. They are not an afterthought bolted onto existing tests.
E2E tests verify technical correctness. UAT verifies business value. They overlap but are not the same.
Every judge must have adversarial test cases that attempt to bypass its checks. A judge that can't catch sophisticated violations is decorative.
A well-written test suite IS the specification. If the tests don't describe the behavior, the behavior is undefined.

anti_patterns.violation: Tests that only cover happy paths (no error, edge, or boundary cases)
UAT that auto-passes without human verification
BDD feature files with no corresponding step definitions (orphan features)
AI-generated tests merged without human review
Step definitions that don't map 1:1 to feature file steps
E2E tests that depend on specific data state (not self-contained)
Tests that mock so heavily they test the mock, not the code
No judge validation tests (judges run unchecked)
Test descriptions that describe implementation, not behavior ("should call fetchUser" vs "should display user profile")
Snapshot tests as primary assertion (lazy testing)
No test for documented anti-patterns in judge XMLs
Flaky tests not quarantined or tracked
Test file naming inconsistent with convention
Missing test coverage for error states in UI components
No visual regression baseline for UAT

judge_validation_layer.requirement: Every judge XML MUST have adversarial test cases that verify the judge catches its documented violations

meta_testing_approach.description: Create code samples that attempt to fool each judge. The judge must correctly identify violations. Track false negatives (missed violations) and false positives (false alarms).

judge.name: design.xml
judge.test: Submit compliant-looking UI with subtle contrast failures
Submit emoji disguised with aria-labels (still an anti-pattern)
Submit pixel-perfect layout with broken tab order

judge.name: state-management.xml
judge.test: Submit React Query usage that silently skips invalidation on one mutation path
Submit Zustand store that looks scoped but leaks UI state into global
Submit derived state that uses useMemo but has stale closure

judge.name: conditional-building.xml
judge.test: Submit permission check disguised as business logic
Submit feature flag with no lifecycle metadata
Submit entitlement check merged into permission guard

judge.name: local-first.xml
judge.test: Submit cache-first pattern disguised as local-first
Submit sync handler that silently overwrites local on conflict
Submit "offline support" that just catches fetch errors

judge.name: backup-management.xml
judge.test: Submit backup script with no schema version in metadata
Submit backup that has never been restore-tested
Submit replication config disguised as backup

judge.name: sync-management.xml
judge.test: Submit webhook handler with no payload validation
Submit sync replication marketed as backup strategy

uat_generation_layer.requirement: UAT is ALWAYS a human-executable checklist, never an auto-passing script

uat_format.description: Generated UAT produces two artifacts: (1) a Playwright script that navigates to each state, (2) a human checklist with expected outcomes the human must verify

uat_rules.rule: Every UAT script uses page.pause() or equivalent to stop for human inspection
Every UAT includes a markdown checklist in the file header
Every UAT includes "edge cases the developer probably missed" section
Every UAT references screenshot baselines when visual verification matters
UAT NEVER contains assertions that auto-pass. Assertions are in the CHECKLIST, not the code.
UAT must be regenerated when the corresponding feature file changes

edge_case_generation.description: For every feature, generate edge cases across these dimensions

dimensions.dimension: Empty, max-length, unicode, RTL, special chars, SQL injection attempts
Offline, slow 3G, timeout, partial failure, CORS error
Simultaneous edits, rapid clicks, back-button during submit
Empty state, error state, loading state, partial data, stale cache
Keyboard-only navigation, screen reader flow, high contrast mode, reduced motion
Expired token mid-action, role change mid-session, concurrent logout

bdd_cucumber_pipeline.requirement: BDD feature files are the single source of truth. Step definitions translate to Playwright. No orphans in either direction.

pipeline_flow.step: 1. Human writes or approves .feature file (Gherkin syntax)
2. AI generates step definitions (.steps.ts) as PROPOSAL
3. Human reviews step definitions for accuracy
5. UAT checklist auto-generated from feature scenarios
6. Human runs UAT and marks pass/fail

feature_file_standards.code:
# features/user-profile.feature # Author: [human] # Last reviewed: 2025-02-05 # UAT generated: uat/user-profile-update.uat.ts
Feature: User Profile Management As a registered user I want to manage my profile information So that my account details stay current
Background: Given I am logged in as a standard user And I am on the profile page
Scenario: View profile information Then I should see my current name And I should see my current email And I should see my avatar
Scenario: Edit profile successfully When I click the edit button And I change my name to "New Name" And I click save Then I should see a success confirmation And my name should display as "New Name"
Scenario: Validation prevents empty name When I click the edit button And I clear the name field And I click save Then I should see a validation error on the name field And the form should not submit
Scenario Outline: Input boundary testing When I click the edit button And I enter "<input>" in the name field And I click save Then I should see "<expected_outcome>"
Examples: | input | expected_outcome | | | validation error | | A | success confirmation | | A name with 500 characters... | validation error | | <script>alert('xss')</script> | sanitized input saved | | Nom avec accents eaigu | success confirmation |

orphan_detection.check: Every Scenario in .feature has corresponding step definitions
Every step definition is referenced by at least one .feature
Step definition count matches feature step count (no dead steps)

criterion.name: Judge Validation Coverage
criterion.grade: No adversarial tests for any judge; judges run unchecked
Some judges have basic tests but no adversarial/evasion attempts
Most judges have adversarial tests; false negative rate unknown
All judges have adversarial tests; false positive/negative rates tracked; evasion attempts documented
Comprehensive adversarial suite per judge; automated false positive/negative tracking; judges improved based on test failures
Generative adversarial testing: AI generates new evasion attempts automatically; judge accuracy is a measured SLI; judges self-improve from adversarial feedback loops

criterion.name: UAT Human-Verifiability
criterion.grade: No UAT exists; or UAT auto-passes without human input
UAT exists but is just E2E tests relabeled; no human checkpoint
UAT has human checklists but no navigation scripts; human must manually find each state
UAT navigates to states + pauses for human verification; checklist with expected outcomes
UAT includes edge cases, screenshot baselines, accessibility checks, and explicit pass/fail per item; regenerates from feature files
UAT is a complete acceptance harness: navigates, pauses, records human decisions, generates pass/fail report, tracks acceptance over time, flags regressions against previous UAT runs

criterion.name: BDD Pipeline Integrity
criterion.grade: No BDD; or feature files exist with no step definitions; or steps exist with no features
Feature files and steps exist but out of sync; orphans in both directions
Features map to steps but mapping is informal; no orphan detection
1:1 mapping enforced; orphan detection in CI; feature files human-authored
Feature files drive step generation; UAT generated from features; orphan detection automated; Playwright execution wired

Living documentation system: feature files are the spec, step definitions are generated and validated, UAT is derived, test reports map back to feature language, stakeholders can read test results in Gherkin

criterion.name: Edge Case Coverage
criterion.grade: Only happy path tested; no error, boundary, or adversarial scenarios
Some error cases but boundaries untested; no adversarial inputs
Error and boundary cases exist for critical paths; gaps in secondary flows
Systematic edge case coverage across input, network, state, and concurrency dimensions
Edge cases generated per dimension matrix; coverage tracked; new dimensions added as architecture evolves
Property-based edge case generation: system automatically discovers boundary conditions; fuzzing integrated; every discovered edge case becomes a permanent regression test

criterion.name: Test Trust Stratification
criterion.grade: All tests treated equally; no distinction between machine-verified and human-verified
Some awareness but no formal stratification; AI-generated tests mixed with human-written
Tests tagged by origin (human/AI) but trust level not enforced in CI
Clear trust tiers; AI-generated tests flagged for review; UAT requires human sign-off; merge rules enforce
Trust tiers in CI pipeline; AI proposals in separate stage; human-verified tests gate deploys; trust provenance tracked
Full test provenance chain: every test has origin, reviewer, last-verified date, confidence score; stale tests auto-flagged; trust decay model triggers re-review

criterion.name: Test-to-Spec Traceability
criterion.grade: Tests exist in isolation; no connection to specs, judges, or feature files
Informal connection; developers know which tests cover which specs
Some tests reference spec documents in comments
Tests tagged with spec references; coverage report maps tests to spec criteria
Bidirectional traceability: spec criterion → test cases, test case → spec criterion; gaps auto-detected
Spec changes automatically flag affected tests; new spec criteria auto-generate test skeletons; traceability matrix is a living artifact updated in CI

criterion.name: Flakiness Management
criterion.grade: Flaky tests ignored or rerun until green; no tracking
Some awareness of flaky tests; manual retry; no quarantine
Flaky tests identified; some quarantined; no root cause analysis
Quarantine process; flaky tests tracked; root cause analysis required before un-quarantine
Automated flake detection; quarantine pipeline; flake rate as a team metric; SLO on flakiness
Zero-flake policy enforced in CI; deterministic test execution; any non-determinism is a bug, not a retry; flake detection in pre-merge

example.description: AI-generated test that rubber-stamps (no adversarial value)
Behavior-driven test with adversarial edge cases

step.details: - Identify test runner(s) (Vitest, Jest, Playwright, Cucumber) - Map test layers (unit, integration, component, E2E, UAT) - Check for BDD pipeline (.feature files, step definitions) - Check for judge validation tests - Check for docs/testing-specs.md
- Does each judge XML have corresponding adversarial tests? - Do adversarial tests include evasion attempts? - Is false positive/negative rate tracked?

- Does UAT exist for critical user flows? - Does UAT pause for human verification? - Does UAT include checklist with expected outcomes? - Does UAT include edge cases? - Can UAT auto-pass? (violation if yes)

- Do .feature files exist for user-facing behavior? - Do step definitions map 1:1 to feature steps? - Are there orphan features or orphan steps? - Are feature files human-authored/approved? - Is UAT generated from features?
- Are tests behavior-driven or implementation-driven? - Edge case coverage across dimensions? - AI-generated tests flagged for review? - Flaky tests tracked and quarantined?
- Adversarial test skeletons for each judge - UAT template for critical flows - Orphan detection script - Update testing-specs.md

output_requirements.requirement: Grade all rubric criteria with evidence
List violations by severity with file references
Generate adversarial test skeletons for each judge
Generate UAT template with human checklist format
Detect orphan features and orphan step definitions
Provide before/after refactors for weak tests

instructions.instruction: AI-generated tests are PROPOSALS. Always flag them for human review.
UAT that auto-passes is ALWAYS a critical violation
Tests that only confirm happy paths are ALWAYS a critical violation
Every judge XML must have adversarial tests or it's flagged as high-severity gap
BDD feature files are human-owned. AI can propose step definitions only.
Edge cases should be generated across all dimensions, not just the obvious ones
Reserve S grades for systems where testing is a self-improving, traceable, human-verified pipeline
Remember: A test that always passes is not a test. It's a lie.

standardization_check.step: Locate test files and identify test runner(s)
Check for adversarial tests per judge XML
Verify UAT scripts pause for human verification (no auto-pass assertions)
Verify .feature files have corresponding step definitions (no orphans)
Verify step definitions are referenced by features (no dead steps)
Verify edge case coverage across input, network, state, concurrency dimensions
Verify AI-generated tests are flagged for human review
Check for flaky test tracking and quarantine process
Verify testing-specs.md exists and cross-references other specs
